annotation.title_clean: Canadian Jurisdictional Guidelines for the Safe Testing and Deployment of Vehicles Equipped with Automated Driving Systems, Version 2.0
annotation.title_en: Canadian Jurisdictional Guidelines for the Safe Testing and Deployment of Vehicles Equipped with Automated Driving Systems, Version 2.0
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA)
annotation.summary_en: Voluntary guidelines from CCMTA (2nd edition, Feb 2022) for Canadian provinces and territories on regulating testing and deployment of SAE Level 3-5 ADS-equipped vehicles. They cover governance committees, test permits, registration, insurance, driver licensing, law enforcement, incident reporting, cybersecurity, data, shuttles, delivery devices, connected vehicles and platooning.
key_provisions_or_claims: Jurisdictions should create an ADS Committee and lead agency to coordinate testing and deployment policy.
Require vehicle-specific test permits with safety assessment against Transport Canada's 13 safety outcomes, insurance proof and driver background checks.
Require incident reports within 24 hours of a collision and periodic disengagement reports during testing.
Adopt SAE J3016 terminology and flag ADS level in registration records for consistency across jurisdictions.
Guidelines are voluntary and aim to enable earliest safe introduction without stifling innovation.
